title: Electroencephalography-based machine learning models for hyperacute detection of large vessel occlusion stroke
summary: EEG symmetry features were used to train machine-learning models for hyperacute large-vessel-occlusion stroke detection. In nested cross-validation across 336 patients, including 16 positive cases, the best observed AUC was 0.85, sensitivity 69% and specificity 86%. The small positive sample and cross-validation design limit the result; improved acquisition is needed before clinical implementation.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models using EEG symmetry features
organization: Amsterdam UMC; Witte Kruis Ambulancezorg; Ambulance Amsterdam; OLVG; Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep; TrianecT BV

evidence.tested: Across two prospective diagnostic studies, nested cross-validation evaluated 336 included patients, of whom 16 had anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion. Naïve Bayes had observed AUC 0.85 (95% CI 0.77–0.93), sensitivity 69% and specificity 86%.
evidence.unknown: Only 16 positive cases were included; nested cross-validation is not prospective evaluation of a locked model. Authors state improved EEG acquisition is needed before implementation.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models used EEG symmetry features to classify suspected large-vessel-occlusion stroke.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
